tasks.short: Arrange travel and go with the team.

steps.what: List stored contest dates and travel fields
Coordinate travel arrangements for away contests
Travel with the team to the contest
Sign the travel plan
File the signed travel plan
outputs: filed copy of signed travel plan v1

tasks.design: A job in {CALENDAR} lists stored contest dates and travel fields. The coach coordinates the travel arrangements and travels with the team. A later job files the signed plan in {DOCS}. It does not buy a ticket.
tasks.previous_blocker: Contest dates were confirmed by a chain of messages.
tasks.enabler_now: Contest date, destination, and party size are already stored.
tasks.still_hard: The coach still travels with the team.
tasks.human_edge: The coach decides the arrangement is complete.
tasks.altitude: The coach spends the week traveling, not on listing dates.

reach.task: Travel only on the plan the coach signed

evidence.claim: The executive digest says casting, game strategy, and judging artistry stay with people.

assumptions: Contest date, destination, and party size are stored on the travel record. The travel record produces them. A blank destination is not booked. Filing the plan does not buy a ticket.
Native configuration of the travel record is used before any custom code.
Only the version the coach signed is filed or sent.
unknowns: Who else must see the signed note.
research_questions: How often the required field is blank.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining count is still the coach coordinating travel arrangements for away contests.

incremental.description: Refresh contest date, destination, and party size when the travel layout changes, and drop a plan the coach has not signed.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes many destinations are blank. The high end assumes contest date, destination, and party size are stored. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: List stored performance records with no fitness score
Evaluate athletes' skills and performance records
Determine fitness and potential in athletics
Sign the fitness judgement
File the signed fitness judgement
outputs: filed copy of signed fitness judgement v1

tasks.design: A job in {DOCS} lists stored performance records and writes no fitness score. The coach evaluates the athletes' skills and determines fitness and potential. A later job files the signed judgement. It does not automate a health judgement and it does not track athletes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Fitness was inferred from a pile of old sheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Athlete identifier and record date are already stored.
tasks.still_hard: The fitness judgement stays with the coach.
tasks.human_edge: The coach decides potential in that area.
tasks.altitude: The coach spends the week on the judgement, not on listing records.

reach.task: Hear only the judgement the coach signed

evidence.claim: Digest [S16] says injury notes are health data. This design does not read injury notes and does not automate a health judgement.
Digest [S17] says tracking a club's own players needs works council consent. This design does not build a tracking dashboard.
The executive digest says ranking players to sign fits that high-risk reading. This design does not rank players.

assumptions: Athlete identifier, record date, and note type are stored on the performance record. The performance record produces them. A row whose stored type is injury is left out and its text is not read. A blank record is not a fitness score.
Native configuration of the performance record is used before any custom code.
Only the version the coach signed is filed or sent.
The coach determines fitness. The job does not rank athletes.
unknowns: Who else must see the signed note.
research_questions: How often the required field is blank.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining count is still the coach evaluating athletes' skills and performance records.

incremental.description: Refresh athlete identifier and record date when the performance layout changes, and drop a judgement the coach has not signed.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes many record dates are blank. The high end assumes athlete identifier and record date are stored. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: List equipment due by the inspection interval
Monitor athletes' use of equipment in person
Ensure the use is safe and proper
Sign the equipment check
File the signed equipment check
outputs: filed copy of signed equipment check v1

tasks.design: A job in {OPS_SYSTEM} lists equipment that is due because the stored inspection interval has passed since the last check. The coach monitors the athletes' use in person and ensures it is safe and proper. A later job files the signed check in {DOCS}. It does not watch athletes with a camera.
tasks.previous_blocker: Due dates were guessed from the last time someone looked.
tasks.enabler_now: Equipment identifier, last check date, and inspection interval are already stored.
tasks.still_hard: Watching the use stays with the coach.
tasks.human_edge: The coach decides the use is safe.
tasks.altitude: The coach spends the week on the floor, not on the due list.

reach.task: Use only equipment the coach has checked

evidence.claim: Digest [S17] says tracking a club's own players needs works council consent. This design does not build a tracking dashboard.

assumptions: Equipment identifier, last check date, and inspection interval are stored on the equipment record. The equipment record produces them. An item is due only when the stored interval has passed since the last check. A blank interval is not due. A blank last check date is not due.
Native configuration of the equipment record is used before any custom code.
Only the version the coach signed is filed or sent.
The list is equipment, not a tracking dashboard of named athletes.
unknowns: Who else must see the signed note.
research_questions: How often the required field is blank.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining count is still the coach monitoring athletes' use of equipment in person.

incremental.description: Refresh equipment identifier, last check date, and inspection interval when the equipment layout changes, and drop a check the coach has not signed.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes many inspection intervals are blank. The high end assumes equipment identifier, last check date, and inspection interval are stored. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Follow changing rules of the sport.

steps.what: List stored rule changes for the sport
Keep abreast of changing rules and techniques
Judge technologies and philosophies relevant to sport
Sign the rule reading
File the signed rule reading
outputs: filed copy of signed rule reading v1

tasks.design: A job in {DOCS} lists stored rule changes for the sport. The coach keeps abreast of the changing rules and techniques and judges which technologies and philosophies matter. A later job files the signed reading. It does not adopt a rule by itself.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rule changes arrived as unmarked clippings.
tasks.enabler_now: Rule identifier, change date, and sport name are already stored.
tasks.still_hard: Judging what matters stays with the coach.
tasks.human_edge: The coach decides which change applies.
tasks.altitude: The coach spends the week on the judgement, not on listing changes.

reach.task: Follow only the reading the coach signed

evidence.claim: The executive digest says casting, game strategy, and judging artistry stay with people.

assumptions: Rule identifier, change date, and sport name are stored on the rule-change record. The rule-change record produces them. A blank change date is not treated as a current rule.
Native configuration of the rule-change record is used before any custom code.
Only the version the coach signed is filed or sent.
unknowns: Who else must see the signed note.
research_questions: How often the required field is blank.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining count is still the coach keeping abreast of changing rules and techniques.

incremental.description: Refresh rule identifier, change date, and sport name when the rule layout changes, and drop a reading the coach has not signed.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes many change dates are blank. The high end assumes rule identifier, change date, and sport name are stored. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The coach spends the week on the field, with the athletes, and on the signed note. A stored list, an unnamed slot, and filing that signature can move. The coach still runs the session, chooses the people, and signs the note.
reach: An athlete trains only on the session the coach signed.
A parent sees only the note the coach signed.
skills_to_grow: Reject a schedule that names a player the coach did not assign.
Reject a scouting claim that does not restate a stored note.
Reject a letter or an order the coach has not signed.
role.ambitious_version: A signed schedule or report can be filed the same day, and the coach still owns the field.
